records.deidentified_narrative: mv1 was stopped at stop sign facing wb on timber path. this corner is very low lit and visibility is difficult in the dark. ped was walking wb on timber path and said he observed mv1 at the stop sign and could not verify if he saw a turn signal on. the driver of mv1 said that she did not see ped on the sidewalk or the crosswalk when she was stopped at the stop sign. mv1 said she continued travel turning nb onto village park and observed ped in the front right corner of her vehicle. ped said that he was walking off the sidewalk and onto the crosswalk before he observed mv1 turning and then was knocked to the ground by mv1. the driver of mv1 said that she crashed into ped. while on patrol, in a marked patrol unit in uniform, i approached the intersection of timber path and village park and observed ped lying on the roadway face up and not moving. the driver of mv1 was outside the driver side door waiting for pd and ems. i announced to dispatch that i was 10-6 and required ems at the scene. when i contacted ped, i observed ear buds in both his ears and they were attached to a mobile device. ped was able to converse with me and was very aware of his surroundings. the driver of mv1 was scared and shaken. she expressed sincere remorse about the crash and wanted to help ped. mv1 driver said, ""this corner is so fucking dark, i just didn't see him."" ems arrived on location. i observed a small bump on the back of ped head and a small scratch on his right elbow. ems point out a small abrasion on ped's right [medical facility] for treatment. mv1 driver was uninjured and very cooperative. i believe that ped may have been inattentive and listening to his mobile too loudly to observe his surroundings. mv1 was inattentive to the roadway and crosswalk and i believe these factors caused the crash. there were on witness on scene. hoa security provided traffic control. coban on.

records.public_safe_text: on [date] at approximately 1645 hours, erika mcdonald was in her dodge journey getting ready to reverse out of her parking spot at the bastrop heb plus. juanita voigt was leaving her vehicle and walking to get a basket. erika looked both ways and did not see any people or vehicles. erika began to reverse out of her parking spot. while reversing, erika heard a slight thud at the rear of her vehicle. erika stopped and looked out her side window. erika saw juniata standing off to the side of her vehicle. juniata walked over to erika and told her that she had hit her with the car. juniata asked for erika’s drivers license. erika provided it and juanita took a photo of the license as well as erika’s tags. juanita asked for erika’s insurance. erika did not feel comfortable at this time and told juanita that she wished to call the police. juanita told erika that she was not that type of person and that the police did not need to be called. juanita walked into the store and erika left the area. erika went to the bastrop police department to report the incident. erika would eventually meet with officers at the heb. at approximately 1712 hours, juniata’s nephew called the bastrop county telecommunications division to report the crash. officers spoke to juniata and erika. juanita was refusing ems evaluation and was reporting that she had pain and discomfort. juanita stated to an officer that she goes to the chiropractor. juniata had no visible injury’s. i inspected erika’s journey and i did not see any marks in the dirt on the rear of the vehicle. information was exchanged between erika and juanita.

[roadway] of traffic facing a red traffic signal intending [roadway]. unit 2, a pedestrian, is standing [roadway] of traffic approximately one foot (1') from [roadway] (according to the oral testimony on scene provided by the driver of unit 1), outside of the fully marked crosswalk boundaries to the south of the intersection [roadway]. the pedestrian is facing a ""do not walk"" icon perpendicular to the moving lanes of traffic of fannin. the driver of unit 1 stated that his vision was obscured to oncoming vehicular traffic traveling southbound on fannin by a steel fence and covered metro bus stop shelter and, in an attempt to fully observe and clear the intersection before turning onto fannin, he maneuvered the patrol vehicle in which he was operating forward approximately nine feet (9') forward and brought it to a complete stop. the driver of unit 1 stated that once he was satisfied that there was no oncoming vehicular and pedestrian traffic from the left, and checking to the right observing the approximate location of the pedestrian as previously stated, he maneuvered the motor vehicle in which he was operating to the right onto the intersection of the [roadway]. the driver of unit 1 stated that he heard something strike the right side of the patrol vehicle. unit 2 (pedestrian) strikes unit 1. the driver of unit 1 stated that he immediately maneuvered the patrol vehicle to the left and brought it to a complete stop, partially in the left center and partially in the right center lanes of traffic approximately thirty and one half feet (30. 5') from the point of impact. the driver of unit 1 stated that he exited from the patrol vehicle and observed the pedestrian lying face [roadway] of traffic and began to render first aid. during the course of the investigation/reconstruction of the scene i discovered that;it appears that the pedestrian (unit 2) intentionally walked approximately five feet (5’) from the point in which the driver of unit 1 initially observed him standing and intentionally striking the right side of the moving patrol vehicle. i observed a distinctive fresh swipe (the distinctive removal of dirt/road grime previously deposited on unit 1) indicating the point of impact, whereas it appeared that the upper leg of the pedestrian made contact with the right quarter panel of the patrol vehicle between the centerline of the front axle and the rearmost of the front right wheel well. it appears that the pedestrian was found in close proximity to the initial reported point of impact as reported by the driver of unit 1, estimated to be approximately three feet (3’) to the south of the point of impact. i also observed that the right hand exterior rear-view mirror of the patrol vehicle was undisturbed, in its original position and not folded in toward the door as one would expect. it is my opinion that the pedestrian intentionally, willingly, and knowingly walked into the patrol vehicle as it passed, perpetrating a fraudulent crash.
